newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down slightly on Thursday due to profit-taking in heavy volume, indicating mixed opinions about the market trend, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 19,500 yuan ($2,349) per tonne, losing 40 yuan. It opened at 19,500 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 19,520 and a low of 19,350.
November fell 50 to 18,990, December 20 to 19,210, January 80 to 19,440, March 40 to 19,500, April 20 to 19,520 and May 80 to 19,520.
Combined volume rose to 87,760 tonnes from 61,620.
Copper opened lower and fell further before heavy speculative buying pushed prices up from lows, but still down from Wednesday's close.
Traders said LME falls after gains in the past few days triggered heavy selling in the morning but most contracts found support at the 19,500-yuan session late in the session.
"Panic profit-taking was responsible for today's falls, but there was speculative buying at low levels due to a lack of further negative news," one trader said.
"This also indicated that many investors were mixed about the direction of the market in the short term," he added.
Traders said technical charts indicated further rises but that they would be limited by over-supply of spot copper.
"Copper will have the chance to test the 20,000-yuan level if it can hold steady above 19,500 yuan," a second trader said.
Analysts said it is difficult to forecast the direction of copper in the short term.
Aluminium ended mixed. November was unchanged at 13,450, December did not trade and January fell 200 to 13,400.
